intro: High above Elazığ, a whole history waits. This is Harput, an ancient city in Elazığ province, lived in from the 2nd millennium BC until today. It is a historic mound and castle town whose story spans Urartu to Ottoman times. Shall we climb in?
history: People have lived here since the 2nd millennium BC. Harput was an important centre under Urartu, Rome, Byzantium, the Seljuks and the Ottomans. Think of it as a book of many pages: a city of 4,000 years lies layered beneath Harput Castle.
structure-1: You are now before Harput Castle, the fortress on the rock above Elazığ. Its story spans Urartu to Ottoman times. Look up, and imagine every age that kept watch from these walls.
structure-3: Here is the Sara Hatun Complex. This Harput complex was built in the name of Uzun Hasan's mother, Sara Hatun, a son's tribute set in stone.
structure-4: Now to the Ice Cave. Even in summer it stays icy, acting as a natural cooler. Can you feel the chill in the air?
structure-5: And here is the Harput Museum, displaying archaeological finds from the Harput region. Inside, the layers of this city come to light.
highlights: As you wander, don't miss the Great Mosque.
facts: Did you know? The dome of Harput's Great Mosque is among the oldest mosque domes in Anatolia. The fortress was used without a break from Urartu to the Ottomans. Its name, 'Milk Castle', comes from a legend that milk was mixed into the mortar instead of water. And one more story: the city of Elazığ was founded when Harput came down to the plain in the nineteenth century. The modern town is the old one, relocated.
outro: This brings our journey through Harput to an end. Before you go, please leave the stones untouched, keep to the marked paths and carry water with you. Thank you for walking with us, and enjoy your visit.
